doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Los Angeles, Chet Baker and film beginnings
title: Just a Child and other tunes recorded by others
summary: Mandel recalls writing Just a Child for Bill Perkins's octet, Getz recording it later, Perkins's Mandel album around 1970, and Hal McKusick's Tommyhawk.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Let’s see at this point…
I don’t remember the Chico Hamilton thing at all…
I’ll have to, I’ll make a…
But thank you Chico, if you made the offer.
[laughs] And you did a little bit of writing for – we talked earlier about that Bill Perkins octet record.
Oh yeah, um-hm.
Did you write, “Just a child,” specifically for that date or you had written that tune…

I guess I did, yeah, that was when the tune happened and then Stan Getz recorded it later, something I never realized until I heard a documentary that they did on Stan after he died, I never realized he recorded that song and it was perfect for him.
Absolutely and then Bill did it again.
Bill did it again?
Yeah, do you know that album he did that’s a totally Johnny Mandel album.
Oh, that one, yeah.
With Victor Feldman and John Pisano.
Oh that's right, yeah.
Around 1970.
I guess so, yeah.
So at that point you did that, Hal McKusick did a recording of, “Tommyhawk,” on that Jazz workshop record.
I guess he did, yeah, these are all, this is like seeing – this must be what dying’s like.
I hope not. [laughs]
I hope so, I’m enjoying this.
I mean the janitor’s gone, if we have a corpse here [laughs] it’s gonna be awfully awkward.
Yeah, but I mean your whole life flashes before your eyes.
